artists.biography:
Andrew John Partridge (born 11 November 1953) is an English singer, songwriter, and record producer who founded the rock band XTC. He and Colin Moulding each acted as a songwriter and frontman for XTC, with Partridge writing and singing about two-thirds of the group's material. While the band were a formative punk group, Partridge's music drew heavily from British Invasion songwriters, and his style gradually shifted to more traditional pop, often with pastoral themes. The band's only British top-10 hit, "Senses Working Overtime" (1982), was written by Partridge.

Partridge is sometimes regarded as the "godfather" of Britpop. Since the 1980s, he has worked, written with, or produced for many other recording artists—efforts which include collaborative albums with Peter Blegvad, Harold Budd and Robyn Hitchcock. From 2002 to 2006, Partridge's APE House record label released several volumes of his demos and songs as part of the Fuzzy Warbles album series. Beyond music, he is a graphic illustrator, toy soldier hobbyist, and designer of board games.

perplexity.description:
Released in June 2018 on Ape House, Apples & Oranges / Humanoid Boogie is a limited-edition EP by Andy Partridge that showcases his enduring affinity for quirky, inventive pop and rock. The album features Partridge’s interpretations of two cult 1960s singles: “Apples & Oranges,” originally by Pink Floyd (written by Syd Barrett), and “Humanoid Boogie,” by the Bonzo Dog Doo-Dah Band (written by Neil Innes). Musically, the EP blends Partridge’s signature melodic craftsmanship with a playful, slightly psychedelic sensibility, reflecting both the spirit of the originals and his own idiosyncratic style. The arrangements are rich and textured, balancing pop accessibility with subtle experimental touches, making it a fitting addition to Partridge’s catalog of solo and collaborative work.

Within Andy Partridge’s discography, Apples & Oranges / Humanoid Boogie stands as a tribute to the eccentric British pop of the late 1960s, a period that has long influenced his songwriting. The EP highlights Partridge’s ability to reinterpret classic material while retaining his distinctive voice, bridging his work with XTC and his solo projects. Although the release was limited and quickly sold out, it received positive attention from fans and critics for its faithful yet fresh takes on these obscure gems. The EP’s commercial reach was modest, but its critical reception underscored Partridge’s status as a respected figure in the world of alternative pop and rock.
